analysis.title: GS TWIG Notes: This Week in Global Research - October 30, 2026
key_insights: GS baseline for 2027 global growth is in line with 2026's pace and with potential growth, but Jan Hatzius sees downside risks building: higher-for-longer energy prices and rates, a fading AI expansion impulse, and possible AI labor disruption. GS expects fewer rate hikes than are currently priced.
US 3Q GDP growth came in above expectations on consumer spending, and core PCE was in line. GS launched its Q4 GDP tracking estimate at +1.8%.
Euro Area: elections next year in France, Italy and Spain could compel greater fiscal spending (Filippo Taddei).
Taiwan: GS raised 2026 and 2027 GDP growth forecasts by 30-40bp on AI-driven activity and the fastest corporate loan growth in almost 30 years, and expects a rate hike cycle to begin in December.
Emerging markets: the energy shock has had a surprisingly muted effect on growth across most countries (Kevin Daly, Ludovica Ambrosino).

China: investment growth slowed to 1.9% in 3Q26. GS now expects property to fall to 8% of real GDP by 2030 from 30% at its peak, a deeper downturn than previously anticipated, though the growth drag should ease gradually.

AI labor impact: Pierfrancesco Mei finds the effect is broadening beyond Tech jobs, and workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs are taking longer than usual to find new jobs, which are typically as exposed to AI as the old ones.
China's push into high-tech and AI industries is likely to create fewer jobs than are lost in the property and services sectors (Chelsea Song).

Fed and ECB both held rates. GS keeps its forecast of one more hike from each in December and none after. A third hike in March is possible if inflation runs higher than expected, for example from higher-for-longer oil.
The BoJ held rates while forecasting higher fuel-driven inflation in 2027. The BoC delivered an as-expected 25bp hike with a hawkish tone on inflation and a higher growth forecast.
Credit (Amanda Lynam): neutral on AI credit, underweight CCCs, prefers single-Bs over BBs.

Coffee (Lina Thomas): GS forecasts coffee prices to keep declining as strong planting yields are realized, but the bumper crop may be short-lived and the narrow breadth of ICE's coffee futures market may keep front-month prices highly volatile.

Brazil after Lula's re-election: upstream oil and gas producers (PRIO, PBR) remain structurally advantaged over downstream distributors (Vibra, Ultrapar). Utilities (Axia, Sabesp, Equatorial) and infrastructure (WEG) offer high real yields. WEG was upgraded to Buy. Irma Sgarz favors retailers MELI, Raia Drogasil and Smartfit.

Global shipbuilding: Chinese shipyards kept their dominant position on strong container and bulker demand, offsetting slightly softer tanker demand. Industrial automation growth is driven by semis, autos, electronics and lithium batteries, with domestic China makers ceding share in 3Q26.
European luxury shows increasing divergence across brands, categories, consumers and regions. In China jewelry, GS favors Chow Tai Fook and Laopu after the gold rally cooled.

Semis: long-term end demand for semi materials is driving capacity investment for 2027-30, implying a tighter future supply shortage and a more constructive pricing and profit outlook for materials makers (Chao Wang).
Memory: a TrendForce expert session supports a positive 2027 DRAM and HBM pricing outlook, and adding meaningful DRAM capacity will be difficult before 2028.

Biotech: ESMO presentations showed targeted therapies and bi-specific antibodies replacing conventional chemotherapy, with growing focus on tolerability and combination synergies. Otsuka, VERA and VRTX all presented positive Ph3 IgA nephropathy data.

AI and cloud demand is outpacing physical infrastructure capacity, creating backlogs that weigh on revenue and push capex higher (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT reviews). Hyperscaler capex is on pace for another record in 2027, but the amount they need to borrow is less than many fear (Gabriela Borges).
SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics say they are sold out through 2028-2029, and INTC said CPU demand could reach a $200bn TAM by 2030.
Metals and mining conference: declining grades, rising capital intensity, permitting complexity and geopolitical fragmentation make the next wave of copper supply harder to deliver.
Three GS ideas: Sumitomo Bakelite (initiate at Buy), GTT (upgrade to Buy) and Synspective (initiate at Buy).

market_movers.rationale: WEG SA upgraded to Buy. Infrastructure and utility names in Brazil offer high real yields.
Sumitomo Bakelite initiated at Buy on AI server adoption, rising heat generation, advanced packaging and LEO satellite communications.
GTT upgraded to Buy as the global LNG containment systems leader, with a competitive moat, asset-light licensing model and Asian shipyard exposure.
Synspective initiated at Buy as a pure-play Japanese SAR satellite operator positioned for rising SAR demand and government investment.
Upstream oil and gas producers PRIO and PBR are seen as structurally advantaged over downstream distributors under current Brazilian policies.
Favored among Brazil retailers for structural growth.

sector_views.rationale: Upstream producers (PRIO, PBR) are structurally advantaged over downstream distributors (Vibra, Ultrapar) under current policies.
Utilities (Axia, Sabesp, Equatorial) and infrastructure (WEG) offer high real yields with clear operational divergence.
Capacity investment for 2027-30 implies a tighter supply shortage and more constructive pricing and profitability.
2027 pricing outlook is positive and meaningful DRAM capacity is difficult to add before 2028.
Favors Chow Tai Fook and Laopu for defensive earnings and structural growth drivers after the gold rally cooled.
Neutral on AI credit, underweight CCCs, prefers single-Bs over BBs.
